fairness_context.claim_boundary: Static or random routing is a legitimate design choice; the finding concerns the released artifact's realized optimization path and its relationship to the paper's training motivation.

references.title: Hash Layers for Large Sparse Models
Taming Sparsely Activated Transformer with Stochastic Experts

evidence: Equation (2) optimizes the robust-MoE parameter set and includes a model loss plus the second-expert regularizer.
The text motivating Assumption 5.3 states that robust training encourages separation between selected and unselected router scores and local route stability.
The paper states that expert and router Lipschitz constants have been optimized during RT-ER.
Algorithm 1 updates the robust-MoE parameter set, but no straight-through estimator, differentiable gate surrogate, or explicit router loss is specified.
paper_audit.scope: The paper treats the router as part of the optimized robust MoE and attributes a router-margin effect to robust training, while leaving the hard-dispatch differentiation mechanism unspecified. The released scripts do not realize that effect. This is not a claim that static routing is invalid or that Theorem 5.4 is unsound.

source_audit.conclusion: All four released training entry points use the shared hard-index Router. Their losses depend on expert outputs selected by integer argmax/top-k indices and expose no differentiable router-score path.
source_audit.scope: Source-level gradient-path conclusion covers all four released training entry points at the pinned commit. Dynamic optimizer-state and cross-epoch tensor evidence does not automatically extend beyond the observed CIFAR-10 RT-ER run.
